title: The Papers: 'Water cheek' and 'Queen Amy's gold rush'
originalTitle: The Papers: 'Water cheek' and 'Queen Amy's gold rush'
content:
The Daily Telegraph says its own investigation has found that Russia has installed secret bases, external with newly-built launch pads for firing its most advanced long-range suicide drones.

The paper says some of them are already being used to attack Ukraine, but that they also pose a long-term threat to NATO allies putting places such as Warsaw in Poland within reach.

The Daily Mail carries a call from campaigners for ministers to close the loophole on a law which allows paedophiles to change their identity.

It highlights the case of a convicted sex offender who has adopted as many as 20 aliases, external which the Safeguarding Alliance says has allowed him to "shield" his criminal past as he formed new relationships.

The Alliance says it has been campaigning for eight years for the current law, which puts the onus on the offender to let the police know they have changed their name, to be tightened. The paper quotes a Home Office spokesperson as saying that protecting the public from dangerous sexual offenders remains "a top priority".

The Guardian says a review into what it calls the growing "youth jobs crisis" will recommend that specialist internships for young people with special educational needs should be put on "turbocharge, external".

The paper quotes Alan Milburn, who's leading the review, as saying that the problem isn't shortage of effort on the part of young people, but a shortage of "opportunities, jobs, and support".

Half of disability claimants, external would be prepared to sacrifice £1,000 a year of their benefits, in exchange for services such as therapy and healthy meals, according to a survey seen by the Times.

The paper says the Good Growth Foundation, an economic think-tank, polled a thousand people. It reports that ministers are set to consider plans to replace financial benefits with other forms of support, later this year.

We are entering a "golden era for dementia research" reports the Daily Express, external. It's been speaking to the Alzheimer's Society, which says that pioneering treatments and tests which were unimaginable even a decade ago are now within reach.

But it quotes the charity's associate director Dr Richard Oakely as saying that the "hard truth" is that delays in diagnosis are stalling progress in the UK.
